title: A new AccountingHub organization has the starting accounts and mappings
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Use a new organization created on the build.
  • Enable AccountingHub for the new organization.
custom_steps:
1. Open Accounting > Account Mappings.
  2. Open Accounting's chart of accounts.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • "Internal: General Internal" maps to 6500 Vehicle Expenses, "No Charge: Warranty" and "No Charge: Goodwill" to 6430 Warranty & Goodwill Expense, "No Charge: Comeback" to 6440 Comeback Expense.

Step 2:

  • The chart holds 6500 Vehicle Expenses, 6430 Warranty & Goodwill Expense and 6440 Comeback Expense; 6400 Shop Equipment Maintenance is still there.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11763 (Story 6, AccountingHub account mapping), story SV-12295 (Story 13, Release day, seeding and migration)

  • S6-R2: “Automatically set up the starting category mappings using AccountingHub's existing chart of accounts. General Internal defaults to 6500 Vehicle Expenses, already in the default chart. Warranty and Goodwill both default to 6430 Warranty & Goodwill Expense, already in the newer chart. Comeback defaults to 6440 Comeback Expense, a new required account (number confirmed by the AccountingHub owner on 2026-11-09). The existing 6400 Shop Equipment Maintenance account remains available for accountants to select where appropriate; it is not an additional starting category. The mapping key should allow a kind (parts, labor) later, so V2 adds rows instead of changing the contract.”
  • S13-R3: “The AccountingHub setup of S6-R2 runs as an operator command, not a deploy migration: organization by organization in isolation, with a list of failures and a verify mode; it runs after the hub release and again at launch. For each organization it reuses suitable accounts (an active expense account whose name matches), creates missing ones (6430 on a legacy chart too, 6440 Comeback Expense), populates every starting-category mapping, preserves valid mappings and resolves number conflicts with a free number. New organizations get the same set from the seeder.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
